title: Defend: HMAC max-buffer overflow returns WC_HW_E (not CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE)
description: When the HMAC accumulation buffer would exceed WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_HMAC_MAX_BUF, the Update path returns WC_HW_E (crypto2dev_port.c:1125), not CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE. A reviewer might suggest CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE as a 'softer' failure to allow software fallback. This is wrong: HMAC SETKEY returns 0 (claiming the key), so wolfSSL's software path ran no ipad/opad schedule and has no accumulated state. A software wc_HmacFinal fallback would compute HMAC with all-zeros key over zero bytes and return it as a valid MAC — an authentication bypass identical to wolfssl-yjw.7. WC_HW_E is the only safe return: it surfaces a hard failure that the caller cannot ignore. Do not change to CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE. The comment at port.h:53 explains this.
